data.why: The app ships its own working examples (a real BD FACSAria PBMC FCS at data/raw/flowio-demo/ and an auto-generated synthetic fixture on first run), so no example data needs to be written; synth-a.fcs is copied out as an extra file a scientist could upload via the sidebar uploader.

goals: Load a flow cytometry sample (bundled real PBMC file or an uploaded FCS) and run the deterministic parse-compensate-transform-cluster pipeline
Inspect the UMAP embedding and per-cluster marker heatmap to identify distinct immune cell populations
Review cluster frequencies and per-cluster marker summary statistics to characterize the sample
Run the deterministic anomaly detector (z-score + IsolationForest) to flag statistically unusual clusters such as debris or dead cells
Build a reproducible, disclaimered LIMS-style report (with file checksum and exact parameters) summarizing the run, without needing an AI key
Check the pre-computed evaluation panel to judge how trustworthy the optional AI interpretation step is before relying on it

review.summary: The tree accurately records the key-free path through FlowScope: reading the evaluation panel, a seeded clustering run, reading UMAP, frequencies, heatmap and table, deterministic flagging, and a provenance-stamped report. Every screen I opened matches its node. It leaves out the AI artifact-vs-real interpretation and the gating suggestion, which the README treats as the point of the tool, so those should be added as key-gated nodes before filing.
